getting-started-introduction--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' # Zweihänder A front-end UI kit for React, documented here in Storybook. Components are plain elements styled with CSS Modules against a layer of CSS custom properties. There is no CSS framework, no primitive library, and one runtime dependency.
**Early stage — not production-ready.** Two components exist (Button, Text Input). No design review has happened beyond the contrast measurements in these docs, and no Figma file has been applied, so the palettes are chosen for contrast rather than designed. **Expect breaking changes on any `0.x` version bump.** Fine to read, install, or borrow the setup from. Not ready to build a real product on top of yet.
## What it is The whole kit resolves against one stylesheet of custom properties. A component never holds a colour, a size or a radius — it reads a token: ```css .button { background: var(--primary); border-radius: var(--radius-control); font-size: var(--text-body); } ``` Three consequences follow, and most of these docs are about them: - **Theming is scoping.** `` redeclares tokens on a subtree; everything inside re-resolves. No context, no re-render, no theme object. - **Rebranding is one file.** Change what `--primary` means and every rule reading it moves. No component is touched. - **There is no build step on your side.** No config, no content scanning, no plugin. It is a stylesheet. ## How to read these docs **[Foundations](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs)** is the substance — colour, type, spacing, radius, elevation, cursors, and the reasoning and measurements behind each. Start with its Overview. **[Components](?path=/docs/components-overview--docs)** is what exists so far, plus the full category list of what does not. **[Patterns](?path=/docs/patterns-overview--docs)** are whole sections assembled from those components, starting with Application UI: copy one into your app and edit it. Each topic has a hand-written page rather than a generated blurb, and they are written as reference docs — what a token is *for*, where its value came from, what the known gotchas are, and how to override it. ## Next **[Installation](?path=/docs/getting-started-installation--docs)** — two ways to consume the kit, and which to pick.

getting-started-installation--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Getting Started/Installation" />

# Installation

Two ways to consume the kit. They ship the same components and the same
tokens; the difference is who owns the source afterwards.

| | Copy-source | npm package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source lives in | your repo | `node_modules` |
| Editing a component | edit the file | fork or override |
| Upgrading | re-run the CLI, review the diff | bump the version |
| Best when | you expect to customise | you want to version-pin |

**Pick copy-source unless you have a reason not to.** The kit is `0.x` and
incomplete; owning the source means a breaking change is a diff you read
rather than one that arrives.

## Copy-source

Components are served in the [shadcn CLI][cli] registry format, so the CLI
copies the source into your project and rewrites its imports to match your
path alias.

[cli]: https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/cli

The project needs a `components.json` — run `npx shadcn@latest init` first
if it has none. Then:

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/tokens.json
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/button.json
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/text-input.json

npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/theme.json
```

Or register the kit once and add components by name:

```json
{ "registries": { "@zweihander": "https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/{name}.json" } }
```

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add @zweihander/button
```

`tokens` only needs adding once — every component depends on it, so the CLI
pulls it in with the first component anyway. Shared helpers (`utils`,
`icon`) resolve the same way, and the npm dependencies (`clsx`, and
`@base-ui/react` for components with behaviour) are installed for you.

Import the token layer once, at your app's entry:

```css
@import "./styles/zweihander-tokens.css";
```

The CLI prints where each file landed; the path above is relative to the
`src` your `components.json` points at.

**If your bundler needs CSS-module types**, add them once — Vite projects
already get this from `vite/client`:

```ts
declare module '*.module.css' {
  const classes: Record<string, string>
  export default classes
}
```

## npm package

```bash
npm install zweihander
```

```ts

import { TextInput } from 'zweihander/text-input'
import { Divider } from 'zweihander/divider'
import { Badge } from 'zweihander/badge'
import { Avatar } from 'zweihander/avatar'

import { Checkbox } from 'zweihander/checkbox'
import { RadioGroup } from 'zweihander/radio'

import { Card } from 'zweihander/card'

import { Combobox } from 'zweihander/combobox'

import { ProgressBar } from 'zweihander/progress-bar'
import { Skeleton } from 'zweihander/skeleton'
import { Link } from 'zweihander/link'
import { Alert } from 'zweihander/alert'
import { EmptyState } from 'zweihander/empty-state'
import { Tooltip } from 'zweihander/tooltip'
import { Popover } from 'zweihander/popover'
import { Modal } from 'zweihander/modal'
import { Menu } from 'zweihander/menu'
import { Breadcrumbs } from 'zweihander/breadcrumbs'
import { Pagination } from 'zweihander/pagination'
import { Tabs } from 'zweihander/tabs'
import { InlineAlert } from 'zweihander/inline-alert'
import { ErrorState } from 'zweihander/error-state'
import { SuccessState } from 'zweihander/success-state'
import { Collapse } from 'zweihander/collapse'
import { Slider } from 'zweihander/slider'
import { Stepper } from 'zweihander/stepper'
import { Sidebar } from 'zweihander/sidebar'
import { Rating } from 'zweihander/rating'
import { Table } from 'zweihander/table'
import { Calendar } from 'zweihander/calendar'
import { DatePicker } from 'zweihander/date-picker'
import { Carousel } from 'zweihander/carousel'
import { ColorPicker } from 'zweihander/color-picker'
import { FileUploader } from 'zweihander/file-uploader'

```

```css
@import "zweihander/tokens.css";  /* the token layer */
@import "zweihander/styles.css";  /* the component styles */
```

**Order matters** — the component styles read the tokens, so `tokens.css`
has to come first. Beyond those two lines there is nothing to configure.

`react` and `react-dom` are peer dependencies. `clsx` is the only runtime
dependency and installs with the package.

## Verifying it works

Render a Button inside a `Theme` and change the accent. If the button
follows, the token layer is loaded and scoping works:

```tsx
<Theme accentColor="violet">
  <Button>Violet</Button>
</Theme>
```

If the button renders unstyled, `styles.css` is missing (npm path) or the
component's `.module.css` did not come across (copy-source). If it renders
styled but in a **serif** face, the token layer is missing — components
declare `font-family: var(--font-sans)` explicitly, and with no tokens
that resolves to nothing.

## Using the theme

Both paths ship the same `Theme` component, which scopes five independent
settings to any subtree:

```tsx
<Theme accentColor="violet" grayColor="slate" appearance="dark" radius="full-rounded" scaling="105%">
```

It writes custom properties, so it nests in either direction — a dark panel
on a light page, or a light island inside a dark one. The full write-up,
including what each setting moves and how to override tokens directly, is
in **[Foundations → Overview](?path=/docs/foundations-overview--docs)**.

## Contributing to the kit itself

```bash
git clone https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander
npm install
npm run storybook
```

Tokens are generated from `tokens/*.json` — run `npm run tokens` after
editing them, never edit the generated files. `npm run tokens:check` and
`node scripts/check-registry.mjs` both run in CI. The
[README](https://github.com/nguucode/zweihander) has the rest.

components-overview--docs.title: Components/Overview
components-overview--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Components/Overview" />

# Components

Single, reusable UI components (atomic design's "molecules"). Reference list: [uiguideline.com/components](https://www.uiguideline.com/components).

Each component lives in `src/components/<category>/`, with its story set to
`Components/<Category>/<Component>`. Categories below — add a component to the
one it fits, or propose a new category if none fit.

| Category | Components |
| --- | --- |
| **Atomic Elements** | Divider ✅, Badge ✅, Avatar ✅, Tag ✅ |
| **Buttons** | Button ✅, Toggle Button ✅ |
| **Controls** | Color Picker ✅, Rating ✅, Slider ✅, Switch ✅, Checkbox ✅, Radio ✅ |
| **Data Display** | Calendar ✅, Table ✅, Accordion ✅, Carousel ✅, Card ✅, Collapse ✅ |
| **Inputs** | Search ✅, Number Input ✅, Text Input ✅, Textarea ✅, File Uploader ✅, Date Picker ✅, Select ✅, Combobox ✅ |
| **Loaders** | Spinner ✅, Progress Bar ✅, Skeleton ✅ |
| **Navigation** | Breadcrumbs ✅, Pagination ✅, Link ✅, Tabs ✅, Stepper ✅, Menu ✅ |
| **Notifications** | Alert ✅, Toast ✅, Inline Alert ✅ |
| **Overlays** | Modal ✅, Tooltip ✅, Popover ✅ |
| **States** | Empty State ✅, Error State ✅, Success State ✅ |

Unchecked = not built yet.

## How a component page reads

Every component page has the same three tabs, after Material 3, so the
answer you need is always in the same place.

| Tab | Answers | What is on it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Overview** | What is it? | One-line description, the main example, a gallery of variants with when to use each, the status, and Resources: the import line, the registry command, the source. |
| **Specs** | How is it built? | Anatomy (the real component with numbered parts), Measurements for every size, Color for every variant, States side by side, and the API table with live controls. Where Zweihänder departs from the reference spec, "Differences from the spec" says how. |
| **Guidelines** | How do I use it well? | When to use it, when to reach for something else, Do and Don't pairs rendered from real stories, and Accessibility: keyboard, roles and states, each line checked by a test. |

Every value on Specs is read live from the tokens, so it follows the theme
in the toolbar and cannot drift from the code. `npm run docs:check` fails CI
when a component page is missing a tab or a required section.

## Behaviour comes from Base UI

Components are styled with CSS Modules over the token layer; their
*behaviour* — focus, keyboard, ARIA — comes from
[Base UI](https://base-ui.com) (`@base-ui/react`) wherever it is more than
trivial. Button uses its `Button` for the focusable-while-loading state;
Toggle Button, the form controls, the overlays, Select, Combobox, Tabs and
Menu are built on its parts.

The reason is the same one that kept this kit from hand-rolling them: a
Modal needs a focus trap, scroll locking, an inert background and correct
restore-focus; Select and Combobox need typeahead, virtual focus and a
listbox ARIA contract; Menu and Tabs need roving tabindex. Those are not
lines of code, they are years of accumulated edge cases in screen readers
and browsers. Base UI is unstyled, so it carries none of that into the
look — the tokens still decide everything you can see.

Two conventions follow from it:

- **`render` instead of `asChild`.** Any component that renders an element
  you might want to replace takes a `render` prop — an element or a
  function — the same as Base UI's own parts and shadcn's.
- **Base UI's change handlers.** Components built on it expose its names:
  `onPressedChange`, `onCheckedChange`, `onValueChange`, `onOpenChange`.
  Components that wrap a real `<input>` (Text Input, Textarea, Search)
  keep the native `onChange(event)`.

Components with no behaviour worth the name — Divider, Badge, Avatar,
Tag — are plain elements and do not import it.

patterns-overview--docs.title: Patterns/Overview
patterns-overview--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Patterns/Overview" />

# Patterns

Whole sections of a screen, assembled from Components (atomic design's
"organisms"). Where a component is a building block, a pattern is a
finished arrangement of them: a page heading, a row of stats, a settings
form.

Patterns are meant to be **copied and edited**, like Tailwind Plus blocks.
They ship through the registry only, not the npm package: install one and
its file lands in your project, next to the components it uses, as code
you own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/page-heading.json
```

Each pattern is a small React component that takes its content as props,
so a variant is usually a matter of which props you pass. The stories show
the variants side by side, and each one is checked for accessibility like
any component.

## Application UI

| Pattern | Variants | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Page Heading](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-page-heading--docs) | Simple, with breadcrumbs and meta, with tabs | ✅ |
| [Stats](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-stats--docs) | Simple, with trend, with icon and link | ✅ |
| [Description List](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-description-list--docs) | Columns, in a card, stacked | ✅ |
| [Form Layouts](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-form-layouts--docs) | Settings sections, stacked in a card, in a modal | ✅ |
| [Data Table Page](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-data-table-page--docs) | Toolbar and pagination, bulk actions, empty result | ✅ |
| [Top Bar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-top-bar--docs) | Search and actions, top navigation links | ✅ |
| [Nav Sidebar](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-nav-sidebar--docs) | Expanded, collapsible, icon rail, plain | ✅ |
| [App Content](?path=/docs/patterns-application-ui-app-content--docs) | Flat surface, blocks on the canvas | ✅ |

These three are the pieces the [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) template places.

## Later

| Category | Typical patterns |
| --- | --- |
| **Marketing** | Hero, header/nav, feature sections, pricing, testimonials, CTA sections, footers |
| **E-commerce** | Product overviews/lists, category filters, shopping cart, checkout, order history, reviews |

templates-overview--docs.content:
import { Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'

<Meta title="Templates/Overview" />

# Templates

Page frames and whole pages, assembled from Patterns and Components
(atomic design's "templates"). Where a pattern is one section of a screen, a template is
the screen: an app shell, a heading, a toolbar and the content, wired
together on sample data so you can click through it.

Templates are meant to be **copied and edited**, like Patterns. They ship
through the registry only, not the npm package: install one and its files
land in your project, next to the patterns and components it uses, as
code you own.

```sh
npx shadcn@latest add https://ontheshore.biz/zweihander/r/projects-template.json
```

Each template is one React component plus a sample data file. The state
(tabs, search, sort, selection) is local, so it runs as it is; replace the
data and the handlers with your own source when you copy it. Every
template is checked for accessibility in light and dark mode, like any
component.

## Application frame

| Template | Shows | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [App Shell](?path=/docs/templates-application-ui-app-shell--docs) | The frame of an app: places the Top Bar, Nav Sidebar and App Content patterns on the Theme's canvas, in a sidebar or top-bar layout | ✅ |

## Object Management

| Template | Shows | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Projects](?path=/docs/templates-object-management-projects--docs) | A list of projects: tabs with counts, search, status filter, sort, bulk archive, a row's activity | ✅ |

## Later

| Category | Typical templates |
| --- | --- |
| **Object Management** | Detail page, edit form, board view |
| **Settings** | Account, team members, billing |
| **Dashboards** | Overview with stats, charts and a recent-activity list |
